reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and the cited paragraphs support it: §3 (restrictions), §11 (bare fee obligation), §14 (confidentiality definition) and §20 (boilerplate) contain no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right running against Sparkling, and no vendor access to Customer systems.

The only certification-type obligation (§17(b)) is a one-off post-termination self-certification of destruction/return with no vendor entry, auditor or system access, so it is not a recurring audit right and does not trigger the AUDIT parameters.

No redline or counterparty comment is appropriate for a compliant finding; inserting frequency/notice/cost machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge the Vendor's rights, so leaving the text unchanged is the correct minimal action.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' regex is expected here — it reflects the absence of any audit clause rather than a defective edit, and the absence of an audit right is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position.

Residual note for the reviewer: the confidentiality definition's reference to 'accounting records for which access is obtained' and the unquoted Schedules A-F should be confirmed as containing no access/reporting mechanism, but the rationale addresses both and nothing in the supplied text contradicts the compliant conclusion.
